Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-10-12 15:00 PT
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Amir Shah (Redwood), Maya Chen (Velora), Carlos Ruiz (Velora), Nora Patel (Velora), Ethan Wong (Velora)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick hosted embeddings and reranking walkthrough, discussed latency targets ~50-150ms for web search, options for prefix caching and compact quantization. Agreed pilot and shared artifacts.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for making time, I'm Jordan with Redwood, 
[00:06] Jordan Lee: joining me is Priya and Amir, we'll keep this as a product demo focused on embeddings + rerank via our hosted API, then walk through console and Optimize suggestions. Maya, do you want to kick off with a quick context of Velora's search problem?
[00:18] Maya Chen: Yeah sure, thanks Jordan. So Velora runs product search for our e‑commerce clients, we have about 6 million SKUs and a pretty spiky query load, lots of tail queries. Our relevancy has degraded after migrations and we tried a hybrid BM25 + dense vector approach. The dense vectors live in a managed vector DB today but we see poor recall on long queries and reordering issues.
[00:40] Carlos Ruiz: Also to add, latency is a top metric. For web UI we need p95 under 300ms ideally, p50 under 120ms. On the platform side we can't afford steady high costs — so cost per query matters.
[00:53] Jordan Lee: Great, exactly the kind we like to dig into. Priya, do you want to frame how Redwood typically approaches this?
[00:59] Priya Nair: Sure. High level — there are two parts: embeddings + retrieval, and then a reranker. For embeddings we host models or you can bring your own; for retrieval we integrate with your vector index (we've seen folks use Pinecone, OpenSearch, Milvus, etc) and then we have a lightweight reranker endpoint that rescoring the top K candidates. The reranker can be hosted or run on dedicated capacity if you need lower latencies.
[01:26] Maya Chen: When you say "reranker endpoint" is that a full sequence model or a small cross-encoder? How expensive is it?
[01:33] Priya Nair: Good question — it's typically a cross-encoder style model that takes the query + candidate pair and outputs a score. It's more expensive per doc than a single-pass retrieval model but since we only score top K (K=10 to 50 usually) it's often cost-effective and improves MRR a lot. We also have quantized variants that reduce token compute; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles based on your throughput.
[01:54] Nora Patel: Do you support on-the-fly hybrid re-ranking or does it require precomputation?
[01:59] Priya Nair: It's on-the-fly. Typical flow: embed query with hosted embeddings endpoint, run nearest-neighbors in your index, fetch top N doc ids and metadata, call Redwood reranker with query+candidate contexts. We support batching across queries and caching of KV prefixes; for product text where documents are fairly static we recommend prefix/KV caching to speed up repeated calls.
[02:24] Ethan Wong: On caching — is the KV cache the same as like an LRU on the server, or do we manage that?
[02:30] Amir Shah: It's server side, automatic — the runtime keeps a KV cache for autoregressive contexts and reuse, it's helpful if you have repeated queries or query prefixes. For rerank which is short inputs it's less necessary but still useful for summary embeddings or metadata.
[02:44] Carlos Ruiz: Security checklist: can you confirm data retention for hosted API, and KMS support? We can't send PII to vendors in some cases.
[02:52] Jordan Lee: Yes — we have configurable retention windows. For hosted API, default retention is 30 days for debugging traces but you can set zero retention. We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and we provide audit logs for requests. We'll send the SOC2 summary and HSM info in the security pack.
[03:10] Maya Chen: Good. Also wondering — any hard limits on sequence length for the reranker? Product descriptions can be long (up to 1,200 tokens).
[03:18] Priya Nair: The hosted reranker supports up to 2,048 tokens; for very long docs we recommend passing truncated or salient snippets and the metadata payload. We have chunking helpers in the SDK. The console has a sample pipeline for chunking + candidate scoring.
[03:35] Jordan Lee: We'll switch to a live demo — Priya, if you want to share screen?
[03:40] [screen shared — console on screen] 
[03:43] Priya Nair: On the console here is our hosted embeddings endpoint — quickstart shows curl and SDK. If you look at the sample repo link in chat (redwood/relevance-examples), you can see embeddings generation, indexing, then reranker call. The reranker endpoint is a POST to /v1/rerank with payload: query, candidate_contexts. (Note: transcript may say /v1/reranker elsewhere.)
[04:10] [04:10] Jordan Lee: Quick note — sometimes the auto transcript writes "re-ranker" as "ree ranker" — ignore that.
[04:15] Priya Nair: In the optimize tab there are recommended batching windows and a suggested quantization profile — for Velora's QPS distribution we recommend dynamic batching with 50ms max latency window and int8 quantization on the reranker. That typically reduces cost by ~2x with small quality loss.
[04:34] Maya Chen: Our average query length is 12 tokens but mid-tail queries are 50+. How aggressive is int8 on quality?
[04:41] Priya Nair: In our internal evals int8 on cross-encoders retains ~98% relative MRR vs fp16 for many architectures, but results vary. Redwood Optimize runs a small A/B on your holdout prompts to quantify this — which we can include in the pilot.
[04:58] Nora Patel: Can you show us an example rerank request/response?
[05:02] Priya Nair: Yep. (typing) Example: POST /v1/rerank body: {"query": "red shoes size 8", "candidates": [{"id":"123","text":"Red running shoe - size 8"}, ...]} Response: scores array with highest first. The SDK has a reorder helper — you pass original doc ids and it returns new ranking and confidence.
[05:29] Carlos Ruiz: Does the reranker return alignment signals, e.g., why a doc scored higher? We have to show explainability to product teams.
[05:36] Priya Nair: We expose token-level logits and attention is not included by default, but we do provide highlight spans when relevant and can return top contributing tokens via a small explain mode. There's a cost tradeoff for that additional debug info.
[05:50] Ethan Wong: How does Redwood integrate with vector DBs? Is there a managed connector or do we call the Redwood API only for scoring?
[05:57] Jordan Lee: Both patterns are common. You can keep your existing vector DB for ANN and call Redwood only for embedding generation and rerank scoring. We also offer managed vector indexes as an add-on — but given Velora already uses a managed index, you'd likely keep it and call reranker on top.
[06:12] Maya Chen: Regarding throughput: our traffic spikes around 2k qps peak in Black Friday windows. What's your strategy for autoscaling the reranker?
[06:21] Priya Nair: For hosted API we autoscale instances and we recommend a hybrid: use hosted for baseline and Redwood Dedicated burst pools for Black Friday or reserved capacity if you want guaranteed p99s. If you need guaranteed capacity we'd propose a Dedicated contract. For spikes you can also use a cheaper fallback model to degrade gracefully.
[06:38] Maya Chen: Cost math — do you have a sample cost per rerank at K=10?
[06:42] Amir Shah: Rough numbers: a medium cross-encoder quantized to int8 is around $0.0008 to $0.002 per document scored depending on model and region; so K=10 is roughly $0.008–$0.02 per query. We'll send a detailed spreadsheet with per-model per-K estimates.
[06:59] Maya Chen: That's helpful to ballpark.
[07:02] Priya Nair: We'll also show a sample dual-pass where we re-rank only top 10 from vector db and fallback to a faster heuristics model if cost constraints hit.
[07:13] [07:13] Jordan Lee: Quick dive — can we look at sample logs from Velora? Maya, you mentioned you could share top queries?
[07:18] Maya Chen: Yes, we can share an anonymized week's worth. We'll check with legal.
[07:23] Carlos Ruiz: On compliance — do you support SSO and SCIM? We need provisioning integration.
[07:28] Jordan Lee: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC is available for console roles. We'll include an admin guide.
[07:35] [screen shows sample code snippet] 
[07:38] Priya Nair: Here is a quick node snippet: const res = await client.rerank({query, candidates}) — returns scores. For batching we use client.rerankBatch([...]) which helps pipeline scoring for 50+ queries.
[07:54] Nora Patel: For A/B tests do you support traffic split and label gathering? We want to test reranker vs baseline for MRR uplift and CTR uplift.
[08:02] Jordan Lee: Yes — we have rollout policies in the console. You can do canary, percentage rollouts and auto-fallback if latency breaches SLO. Also built-in evals to track quality drift against a labeled set.
[08:16] Maya Chen: Let's talk about evals — how would Redwood run the initial offline eval?
[08:21] Priya Nair: We usually take a seed set of ~2–5k queries with ground truth, run retrieval+rerank offline, compute MRR/Recall@K/CTR proxies. Optimize produces recommended model and quantization per workload. We can run that as part of the pilot — 48–72 hour turnaround typically.
[08:38] Ethan Wong: Any caveats on embedding model drift? If we pick a new embedding model mid-year will indexing have to be redone?
[08:45] Priya Nair: Yes reindexing is required if embeddings change; Optimize can help pick a model family that's stable. We also provide staged rollouts for index rebuilds and incremental reindexing helpers.
[08:58] Maya Chen: About the quickstart — can we see the console's pipeline visual?
[09:02] [09:02] Priya Nair: (scrolling) Pipeline shows: embed -> ANN index call -> candidate fetch -> rerank -> respond. Each node has metrics and cost estimate. You can click the rerank node to see per-call latency breakdown and token usage.
[09:22] Carlos Ruiz: For cost control, do you support per-route quotas? We want to limit the number of rerank calls from internal tools.
[09:28] Jordan Lee: Yes per-route quotas and token budgets per API key. Also alerting when spend approaches thresholds.
[09:35] Maya Chen: I'm thinking about the user experience — some of our queries are conversational, like follow-ups. Does Redwood support conversation-aware reranking?
[09:43] Priya Nair: We do — you can pass conversation context and we maintain KV cache for prior turns. The reranker will score candidates against the full context. For long conversations we suggest only including recent turns to bound tokens.
[09:56] Nora Patel: Any gotchas with multilingual product descriptions? Velora has ~12% non-English content.
[10:02] Priya Nair: Most embedding models supported are multilingual. For reranking multilingual cross-encoders we recommend language-specific models for best accuracy, Optimize will surface recommendations per-locale.
[10:14] Jordan Lee: Let's simulate a quick end-to-end example with the sample dataset in the demo repo — small dataset of 500 products. I'll trigger a sample query.
[10:21] [10:21] Priya Nair: (runs sample) Query "waterproof hiking boot size 10". The retrieval step returns 25 candidates from the index in 40ms, reranker scores top 10 in 110ms, total end-to-end about 160ms from our hosted endpoint.
[10:38] Maya Chen: That's impressive for hosted. Is that under light load?
[10:42] Priya Nair: This is single query local demo; under realistic loads we hit different batching characteristics — Optimize will recommend batch windows to balance latency and throughput.
[10:52] Carlos Ruiz: On telemetry — where do we see token-level cost per call?
[10:56] Jordan Lee: The console usage page shows cost breakdown per model, per API key and per route. You can export per-token cost via CSV.
[11:04] Ethan Wong: Any integration for streaming rerank responses or partial results?
[11:09] Priya Nair: Rerank responses are typically synchronous since they're scoring; we can stream if you want partial candidate updates but for most search patterns a single response is returned.
[11:20] Maya Chen: Let's discuss pilot scope and acceptance criteria. We want 2 week pilot that demonstrates MRR uplift vs baseline and meets p95 latency under 300ms for interactive queries.
[11:29] Jordan Lee: That's reasonable. Pilot plan: 1) Redwood runs offline eval on provided logs (2–3 days), 2) we set up hosted trial keys, SDK quickstart (1 day), 3) run live A/B for 1 week, measure MRR/CTR/p95 latency — report at the end.
[11:46] Maya Chen: Acceptance: >=5% MRR uplift or no regression and p95 <=300ms. If both met we discuss a Dedicated commit.
[11:55] Jordan Lee: Sounds good — we'll document that in the pilot doc.
[11:58] Nora Patel: Few practical questions — do you keep a per-request debug trace we can turn on?
[12:03] Priya Nair: Yes debug traces are available for a subset of calls and can be disabled. They include token counts, latencies per step, and model variants used.
[12:14] Carlos Ruiz: Any network/VPC peering for hosted? We can't expose internal index endpoints to public internet.
[12:20] Amir Shah: For hosted we do not require exposing your index; typically you'd put an ingress layer or use a private connector. For Private deployments or Redwood Dedicated we can do VPC peering or on-prem deployment for strict networks. We'll include the network patterns doc.
[12:36] Maya Chen: Ok I'm happy with next steps. A couple of immediate asks: pricing + pilot cost estimate and the benchmark template.
[12:43] Jordan Lee: We'll share both. Priya, anything to add?
[12:46] Priya Nair: I'll add the sample rerank SDK snippet and the quickstart repo link in the notes. Also I'll kick off a small Optimize job on a sample dataset once we get the logs.
[12:57] Ethan Wong: One more — what about model drift monitoring? We need alerts if quality drops.
[13:02] Jordan Lee: Built-in quality monitoring tracks eval metrics over time and we can alert when MRR degrades beyond thresholds; we also have regression alerts tied to labeled prompt sets.
[13:14] Maya Chen: Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[13:17] Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan will share pricing + benchmark spreadsheet; Priya will send quickstart repo, sample SDK snippet, and console links; Velora to provide anonymized query logs; schedule POC kickoff 2026-10-19.
[13:33] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[13:35] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and setup.

[13:40] End of meeting.
